newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO/Bund spread seen high ahead auction.
newsitem.headline: OLO/Bund spread seen high ahead auction.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds ended lower with other markets on Thursday after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan signalled in a speech to congress that U.S. rates may be hiked next week.

OLO futures, already down more than 30 bp before Greenspan's speech, fell further to close 46 bp lower at 119.95. One chartist said that the 120 point support line could now become a resistance level in the coming trading days. He added that much would depend on whether Bund futures could hold above 99.30 and 99.00 support.
Ten-year OLO yields ended at 6.12 percent, from 6.05.
Their spread over Bunds widened to 16 bp from 13 on Wednesday and is not seen narrowing back to the 10 bp level ahead of the monthly OLO auction on Monday.

"When rates are rising, the OLO/Bund spread always tends to edge out a bit," said Petercam economist Geert Noels. He said that there was enough liquidity in the market to bring the srpead back to 10 bp, but added that buyers did not really appear below the 15 bp level.
Dealers said the market was not nervous about this weekend's review of the 1997 budget, where the government is set to decide on up to 15 billion francs worth of austerity measures.
Short-term yields remained well above the 3.00 percent central rate as doubts about EMU continued.
"As long as this lasts, short rates will remain around the 3.5 percent level," one dealer said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
